actionThatDiffers: Instead of discovering blocked sessions one at a time over an hour, I sit down once and answer all five queued prompts in a single pass, so agent idle time between my answers collapses.
why: Enumerating which panes are blocked is a tmux capture-pane loop away and Claude needs-input is detectable, so an adequate approximation is reachable (rule 2/3 cap); the queue is an ordering over visible inputs. Real behaviour change: one context switch replacing five.

actionThatDiffers: I notice a finished or blocked cloud run within a minute and reply to it, instead of leaving it parked in a browser tab I forget to refresh for an hour.
why: Today it is literally two places: my terminal tabs plus one browser tab on the web app session list, each one click I already know. Annoying, not inaccessible. Delta is coverage and timeliness of cloud runs, a mild convenience most days.

actionThatDiffers: When /usage shows the 5-hour window nearly gone, I kill the one runaway session that is consuming it and keep the other four running, instead of stopping everything or guessing wrong and killing the session I actually needed.
why: Quota is reported globally only, never attributed to a session; per-session burn is not on screen in any harness, so the inputs are not individually visible and rule 3 does not cap it. Correlating token counts in transcript files against a global quota figure is not something I would do reliably mid-crunch. Attribution rests on a heuristic. Prevents a blown quota window, which is concrete loss.

actionThatDiffers: Retrospectively I route a class of cheap work (doc edits, lint burndown) off the expensive model after seeing what those runs cost, but nothing about my current session changes.
why: For the Claude pane I am in, /cost is one command in a place I know. Across 3-12 sessions on several harnesses it means visiting each pane, and most harnesses report no cost at all, so it lands mid. Impact is weak and delayed: interesting number, the decision it feeds is occasional and I can already approximate it from turn counts.

actionThatDiffers: I answer the session that has been stalled 40 minutes before the one stalled 2 minutes, so the longest-idle agent restarts first; I also spot the one that has been blocked since before lunch and would otherwise sit all afternoon.
why: Judged as if unshipped. The prompt is visible in the pane but never its age. A tmux loop over pane_activity/window_activity timestamps gives an adequate approximation in one pass, which caps this at 60 per rule 2. Impact is ordering plus catching the very old one; I was going to answer them all anyway.

actionThatDiffers: Before kicking off the big multi-file refactor I see it will not fit the window and instead start a small bounded task now, doing the refactor after reset, rather than abandoning it half-done when the quota wall hits.
why: Needs remaining quota (easy, /usage or Barista) times a forward burn-rate projection times a size estimate for work not yet started. No harness projects burn forward and nothing estimates task cost, so two of three inputs do not exist anywhere; near-unobtainable by hand, and the value rests entirely on the prediction being right. Prevents wasted hours of half-finished work.

actionThatDiffers: I hand four related sessions to one orchestrated workflow with gates instead of personally remembering which of the four needs my input next, so the hand-orchestration I was doing in my head stops.
why: Kind is action: the thing I do is type a commission prompt, and a workflow-commissioning skill already exists, so doing it today is one prompt (21-40 band). The suggestion is the only new part and suggestion is not the work. Impact is real when it fires but it fires occasionally, not on a regular decision cadence.

actionThatDiffers: Nothing pings me for 90 minutes and I read the suppressed queue afterwards, rather than either eating the interruptions or missing them entirely because I turned the OS mute on and forgot.
why: Kind is action: flipping an existing toggle. macOS Focus / Do Not Disturb is one click and already does the suppression, so access is firmly in the one-click band. The delta over OS mute is only that the notifications are held and replayed rather than lost, which is mild convenience.

actionThatDiffers: On its own, none: I can look up what a session did last Tuesday instead of guessing. Every real decision it enables (burn projection, interrupt counts, digests) belongs to the items it unblocks, not to the log itself.
why: No harness keeps queryable cross-session history. Raw material half-exists (Claude transcript JSONL, git log), so a determined grep gets fragments, but assembling a consistent cross-harness record over time is exactly the correlation-across-time I would not do reliably. Capped at 50 by rule 1: it is an enabler and I cannot name a distinct action that follows from having it alone.
